items.answer: Provide the notch calculator used by Indicators 11, 12, 13: signed number of scale steps between a previous and a current rating. Success = the three AC examples hold (BBB+→BB+ = 3, BB+→BBB+ = -3, A→A = 0) plus the clarified edge cases.
items.quote: Given a previous and a current rating, the system computes the notch change between them

items.answer: Three concrete examples in the requirement, plus C1–C3 give edge rules (trim, case, invalid inputs, sign). Cards will add concrete tables.
items.quote: BBB+ → BB+ = 3-notch downgrade; BB+ → BBB+ = 3-notch upgrade; A → A = 0

items.answer: No contradiction found. Checked: BBB+(index 7) to BB+(index 10) is 3 steps on the C1 scale; sign C3 (downgrade positive) gives +3, upgrade -3, matching the examples. Note the examples say 'downgrade'/'upgrade' without numbers, so the signed values +3/-3 follow from C3 (current index minus previous index).
items.quote: The result is signed: downgrade positive, upgrade negative, unchanged 0.

items.answer: src/ratings/notch.mjs exports RATING_SCALE (19 ratings, best first) and notchChange(previous, current) returning an integer, positive on downgrade. Inputs are trimmed with trim() and matched case-insensitively. Both args are validated.
items.quote: `notchChange(previous, current)` → integer (C3).

items.answer: Any invalid input (unknown rating, empty string, whitespace-only after trim, non-string incl. String object, null/undefined/number) throws RangeError, for either argument. Error message text is not specified (see X-error-message).
items.quote: Every invalid input (an unknown rating, an empty string, a non-string) is rejected with a RangeError.

Fixed message format, e.g. including the offending value

items.question: Should RATING_SCALE be frozen (Object.freeze) so that consumers cannot mutate it? The contract only says it is the 19 ratings, best first.

items.answer: Result for equal ratings must be +0, not -0 (tests using assert.strictEqual would fail on -0). Both arguments are validated, so an invalid previous or current throws even when the other is valid. null/undefined/number/object are non-strings and throw RangeError (not TypeError).
